# Fairstay Payables Review (`fairstay-payables-review`)

Accounts payable review for nursing homes: vendor bank account changes, duplicate invoices, vendors not on the approved list, invoices over the purchase order, missing purchase orders, past-due bills and goods received but not invoiced for the month-end accrual. Bank account numbers are masked before results reach the model.

**Fairstay Payables Review never releases payments or changes vendor bank details.**

Fairstay ver 1 · Financial services · MIT · Node 20 or newer · local files only · resident and staff identifiers masked before results reach the model · built on [`fairstay-core`](../fairstay-core)

```bash
npx -y fairstay-payables-review demo
npx -y fairstay-payables-review mcp --root ./facility-files
```

## What the sample data shows

A fictional Cedar Hollow AP register reviewed on 31 March 2026. Planted:

- Lone Star Linen invoice LL-2201 entered twice.
- Prairie Medical Supply invoice PM-8810: 6380 on a 5500 PO and 19 days past due.
- Gulf Coast Pharmacy asks for payment to a bank account that is not the one on file.
- City Power and Light has no PO, but it is PO exempt.
- Hilltop Floor Care is not an approved vendor and has no PO.
- Bluebonnet Food Service has no PO for 4200.
- PO-904 was received on 28 March with no invoice yet, so it is accrued.

Bank account numbers are listed in [`phi-canaries.json`](fixtures/phi-canaries.json); they must never reach the model. [`rules-typo.json`](fixtures/rules-typo.json) misspells a setting, so the check refuses it.

## Tools

| Tool | What it does | Policy |
|---|---|---|
| `payables_check` | Review the AP register before the check run: holds first, then past due and accruals. | runs |
| `payables_write_report` | Write payables.csv (one row per item, with blank owner and decision columns) and payables.html into out_dir (default evergreen-out/payables). | runs |
| `payables_recall` | Search this agent's own memory of the customer's setup: accepted facts (in use) and facts waiting for a person. | runs |
| `payables_learn` | Propose one fact about the customer's setup for this agent to remember. | runs |
| `payables_accept_learning` | A named person accepts or rejects a fact waiting in this agent's memory. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `payables_retire_memory` | A named person stops an accepted fact from applying. | one named click, even in Auto (`accept_learning`) |
| `payment_release` | Fairstay Payables Review never releases payments or changes vendor bank details. | refused |

Any tool name not in this table is blocked, including names a model invents. Refused tools are listed so a model can see they exist and are refused.

### `payables_check` arguments

| Argument | What it is |
|---|---|
| `invoices` (required) | AP invoice register under --root: vendor, invoice number, dates, amount, PO, paid date, remit bank account |
| `vendors` (required) | Vendor master under --root: vendor, approved, bank account on file, PO exempt |
| `pos` | Optional purchase orders under --root: PO number, vendor, amount, received amount and date |
| `rules` | Optional rules JSON: po_required_over, po_tolerance_pct |
| `as_of` | Review date (YYYY-MM-DD, default today) |
| `status` | Only items with this status |
| `limit` | Most items to return to the model (the report file always has all of them) |

## Columns it reads

Tables can be CSV, TSV, semicolon- or pipe-separated text, Excel `.xlsx`, JSON or JSONL. Columns are matched by the names below (any case and punctuation), and by their usual names in German, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Italian, Japanese, Chinese and Korean. Dates become `YYYY-MM-DD`. Columns marked *masked* hold resident or staff identifiers.

The PointClickCare, MatrixCare and American HealthTech style names were written from public help pages and general knowledge, **not checked against real exports**. Run `npx fairstay-payables-review inspect <file>` (column names and shapes only, never values) and name any column it misses in `remedy-sources.json`.

### AP invoices (`invoices`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `vendor` (required) | text | Vendor, Vendor Name, Supplier, Payee, Remit To |
| `invoice_no` | text | Invoice, Invoice #, Invoice Number, Inv No |
| `invoice_date` | date | Invoice Date, Inv Date, Date |
| `due_date` | date | Due Date, Due, Pay By |
| `amount` (required) | amount | Amount, Amt, Total, Balance, Net Amount, Payment Amount, Paid, Paid Amount |
| `po_number` | text | PO, PO #, PO Number, Purchase Order |
| `paid_on` | date | Paid On, Paid Date, Check Date, Payment Date |
| `bank_account` | text (masked) | Bank Account, Account Number, Remit Account, ACH Account, Bank Acct |

### Vendor master (`vendors`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `vendor` (required) | text | Vendor, Vendor Name, Supplier, Payee, Remit To |
| `approved` | text | Approved, Active, Status, Approved Vendor |
| `bank_account` | text (masked) | Bank Account, Account Number, Remit Account, ACH Account, Bank Acct |
| `no_po` | text | No PO, PO Exempt, Recurring, Utility |

### Purchase orders (`pos`)

| Column | Type | Read from |
|---|---|---|
| `po_number` (required) | text | PO, PO #, PO Number, Purchase Order |
| `vendor` | text | Vendor, Vendor Name, Supplier, Payee, Remit To |
| `amount` | amount | Amount, PO Amount, Total, Approved Amount |
| `received_amount` | amount | Received, Received Amount, Received Value |
| `received_on` | date | Received On, Receipt Date, Received Date |

## Settings file (`payables_rules`)

A small JSON file you pass by path. A misspelled setting is refused by name rather than ignored, so a typo never silently changes a check.

| Setting | What it does |
|---|---|
| `po_required_over` | Invoices at or above this amount need a PO unless the vendor is PO exempt (default 1000) |
| `po_tolerance_pct` | Allowed overage on a PO, percent (default 5) |

## Memory

`payables_learn` only proposes a fact; nothing changes until a named person accepts it with `payables_accept_learning`, which is one click even in Auto. Facts live in a hash-chained file under `.remedy/memory/`; if the chain does not verify, no fact is used. Credentials, personal identifiers and text that reads like instructions to an AI are refused.

| Kind | What an accepted fact does |
|---|---|
| `vendor_note` | is shown with results. It never changes a check. |

## Install

Node 20 or newer. No other runtime dependencies besides `fairstay-core` and `fairclaim-core`.

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "fairstay-payables-review": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": [
        "-y",
        "fairstay-payables-review",
        "mcp",
        "--root",
        "/path/to/facility-files"
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

Claude Code: `claude mcp add fairstay-payables-review -- npx -y fairstay-payables-review mcp --root .`, or use the plugin files in this folder.

## CLI

```bash
fairstay-payables-review tools                 # every tool, its policy and arguments
fairstay-payables-review sources               # the columns each input is read from
fairstay-payables-review inspect <file>        # how a file would be read (names and shapes, never values)
fairstay-payables-review call payables_check '{"invoices":"<invoices>","vendors":"<vendors>"}'
fairstay-payables-review eval                  # the private eval cases on the fictional fixtures
fairstay-payables-review demo
```

## Resident and staff data

Results go to an AI model, so identifiers are masked before they leave the agent: resident and staff names become stable pseudonyms such as `PT-3f9a1c2e`, record and account numbers become `MRN-…` or `ACCT-…`, and e-mails and phone numbers are removed, also inside free text. Report files written to disk keep real names because staff work from them: keep them in a folder only your staff can open. The shared tests check that no fictional identifier from the fixtures reaches any eval result, and the hostile-input check plants spreadsheet formulas, HTML and AI-aimed instructions in the data. This keeps PHI away from the model; it is **not** a HIPAA compliance determination. Your business associate agreements, access controls and policies still apply.

## Limits

- Reads only the files you give it. It does not log in to PointClickCare, MatrixCare, a payer portal, a bank, a state Medicaid portal or a payroll system.
- Medicare, Medicaid and payroll rules are summarised from public material as of 2026 and the numbers are settings you supply; a billing, payroll or legal professional checks them before you rely on them.
- Not legal, tax, accounting, clinical, reimbursement or HIPAA advice. A person decides what to bill, pay, appeal, file or send.
- Every call is written to a hash-chained audit log under `.remedy/` in the root. No network calls, no telemetry, no credentials. The bundled data is fictional.
